title: Kernel kitchen-sink: morning triage & perf todos (Raphael)
content:
Quick scratchpad for the morning triage — noisy p99 on 3/12-3/13, obs in us-west, suspected KV cache churn + microbatching regression. Rapid notes, commands, and hypotheses so I don't forget while I cycle through debug windows.

Observations:
- Time window: spikes started ~2026-03-12 21:10 UTC and recurred every ~15–20m.
- Affected path: /v1/generate (long-form chat) on model: redwood-open-13b-quant.
- Symptoms: token latency spikes from baseline ~80ms -> bursts up to 800–1200ms for a subset of requests. CPU and GPU load looked normal.
- Host-level: nvlink and PCI IO stable, no obvious memory pressure on GPU (util ~55–70%).
- Kernel logs: sporadic "kv_cache_eviction" warnings interleaved with batch scheduler resends.
- Canary: traffic routed to us-east and eu-west not showing same pattern.

Immediate triage done:
- [x] Collected flame graphs from process pid 7124 (snapshot at spike).
- [x] Grepped logs for "kv_cache_eviction" and pulled 30 surrounding requests.
- [ ] Reproduce locally with long-context load generator (next).
- [ ] Run microbatch experiment (batch-size override to 1) on a dedicated rep to see if spikes go away.

Hypotheses:
1) KV cache TTL/eviction is mis-tuning with new prefix caching logic introduced in PR 856 (recent rollout). Eviction kicks in for certain token-length distributions and causes cache misses + additional compute.
2) Batch scheduler intermittently creates an oversized batch due to a race between priority queue update and request cancellation, increasing latency for co-batched short requests.
3) Kernel pinning / NUMA policy: some requests land on suboptimal CUDA streams under contention (less likely given stable GPU util but keep in mind).

Quick reproducible checks to run:
- Re-run load script: tools/loadgen/long_context_runner.py --model redwood-open-13b-quant --seq-len 2048 --qps 25 --duration 10m (capture p99).
- Force kv cache disabled: export RW_KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false; restart runtime on staging-rep-03; run same load.
- Override microbatcher: curl -X POST http://staging-config.local/override -d '{"microbatch.max_inflight":1}' (watch for queuing/backpressure logs).
- Capture 'batch.size' histogram and 'kv.cache.hit_rate' metric for the period.

Useful grep/commands:
- sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -o cat | grep -i kv_cache_eviction -n | sed -n '1,120p'
- curl 'http://metrics:9090/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(batch_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))'
- docker exec -it runtime sh -c "pipenv run python -m tracing.dump_flame pid 7124 > /tmp/flame-7124.svg"

Notes from flamegraph:
- Heavy time in 'kv_lookup' and 'serialize_prompt' during spikes. 'kv_lookup' stack shows many lock acquisitions in fastpath.
- There's an unusual caller: 'batch_scheduler::coalesce_if_ready' which is higher in the stack during spikes.

Short-term playbook (today):
- Priority 1: repro in staging + isolate whether disabling KV cache removes spike (if yes, add telemetry to better correlate requests leading to eviction).
- Priority 2: run microbatch=1 on a canary of 10% for 1 hour, monitor p50/p90/p99 and CPU/GPU overhead.
- Priority 3: add an ad-hoc metric: kv.cache.eviction_rate_by_prefix and a label by request-length_bucket.
- Priority 4: if reproduction fails, capture full request headers for affected requests and check client-side interleaving (tooling: trace-id extraction).

Todo checklist (personal):
- [ ] spin up local loadgen and reproduce (estimate 2h)
- [ ] open follow-up ticket with reproduction steps and attach flamegraphs (JIRA template: perf-investigation).
- [ ] ask Lina to double-check the PR 856 config diff for ttl defaults and any conditional toggles.
- [ ] quick patch: increase kv cache default retention from 60s -> 180s on staging and observe (rollback plan ready).
- [ ] validate microbatch batching logic unit test to cover race with cancellation (create small unit test in serving-runtime/test/batching).

Unresolved questions / checks:
- Which client request patterns cause cache thrash? short-high-rate vs long-low-rate? Need request histogram by prompt tokens.
- Are we seeing correlated retries from frontend that amplify transient misses? Check edge logs for 429/retry loops.
- Does PR 856 change the eviction algorithm (LRU -> TTL-based) or just thresholds? Need to read the diff again.

Context snippets / links I will paste into the ticket:
- Observed log sample (redacted):
  [2026-03-12T21:11:04Z] warn kv_cache_eviction prefix="user:ctx:abc123" reason="ttl_expired" size_before=423 size_after=389
  [2026-03-12T21:11:04Z] info batch_scheduler coalesce_if_ready took=14ms batch_size=23
  [2026-03-12T21:11:04Z] info request trace_id=tr-9f4a token_count=145 lat=980ms

- Dev notes: be mindful that disabling KV cache increases token compute cost ~+12% on staging; we only do short experiments.

Reminders:
- Ping Marcus to check whether the kernel change in commit 2f9b7 altered lock granularity on kv_store (might explain lock contention).
- Standup bullets for today: main focus on reproducing p99 in staging and trialing microbatch reduction.

Misc brain-dumps:
- If eviction / cache misses are root cause, longer-term: consider a 'hot-prefix' pinning mechanism where top-N prefixes are pinned to avoid churn under bursty traffic.
- Also explore a probabilistic caching policy: keep entries that have >X hits in last Y seconds.

End scratch — will update after repro steps or new traces.

Signed-off: R.M.
